16.2.1.2 Nomenclature of Cycloalkanes

Cycloalkanes are alkanes that contain a ring of three or more carbons. Cycloalkanes are named by placing the prefix “cyclo–” to the name of alkane having the same number of carbon atoms as in the ring. For convenience, cycloalkanes are represented by geometric figures e.g. cyclopropane is represented by a triangle, cyclobutane by a square, cyclopentane by a pentagon, cyclohexane by a hexagon and so on. Each corner of these geometric figures represent a –CH₂– group.

Monosubstituted cycloalkanes are named as alkylcycloalkanes. For polysubstituted cycloalkanes, the prefixes di–, tri– etc. should be used to represent the number of identical substituents. Their positions are specified by numbering the carbon atoms of the ring in the direction that gives the lowest number to the substituents at the first point of difference.

When the ring contains fewer carbon atoms than an alkyl group attached to it, the compound is named as an alkane and the ring is treated as a cycloalkyl substituent.

ایک متبادل گروہ والے سائیکلوالکینز کا نام الکائل سائیکلوالکین رکھا جاتا ہے۔ کئی متبادل گروہوں والے سائیکلوالکینز میں یکساں متبادل گروہوں کی تعداد ظاہر کرنے کے لیے ڈائی–، ٹرائی– وغیرہ سابقے استعمال کیے جانے چاہییں۔ ان کی جگہیں حلقے کے کاربن ایٹموں کو اس سمت میں نمبر دے کر بتائی جاتی ہیں جو اختلاف کے پہلے مقام پر متبادل گروہوں کو سب سے کم نمبر دے۔

Other examples

16.2.1.2 Nomenclature of Cycloalkanes

Cycloalkanes are alkanes that contain a ring of three or more carbons. Cycloalkanes are named by placing the prefix “cyclo–” to the name of alkane having the same number of carbon atoms as in the ring. For convenience, cycloalkanes are represented by geometric figures e.g. cyclopropane is represented by a triangle, cyclobutane by a square, cyclopentane by a pentagon, cyclohexane by a hexagon and so on. Each corner of these geometric figures represent a –CH₂– group.

Monosubstituted cycloalkanes are named as alkylcycloalkanes. For polysubstituted cycloalkanes, the prefixes di–, tri– etc. should be used to represent the number of identical substituents. Their positions are specified by numbering the carbon atoms of the ring in the direction that gives the lowest number to the substituents at the first point of difference.

When the ring contains fewer carbon atoms than an alkyl group attached to it, the compound is named as an alkane and the ring is treated as a cycloalkyl substituent.
